2609.27032.abstract: Faithfulness is a central concern in legal text summarization, which motivates extractive approaches that select verbatim content traceable to its source. Such methods typically rank paragraphs or other structural units in isolation, yet give little attention to consolidating evidence that is distributed across, and shares salience between, distant parts of a document. We introduce LexLattice, an extractive summarizer that reifies a legal act's hierarchy as a two-dimensional semantic lattice and consolidates over it with a masked 2D neural cellular automata before selection. LexLattice attains state-of-the-art ROUGE across all 24 languages of EUR-Lex-Sum in both multilingual and cross-lingual settings, surpassing instruction-tuned baselines with billions of parameters, despite concentrating all trainable capacity in a 1.8M parameter consolidator over a frozen multilingual encoder. A consolidator trained only on high-resource languages further transfers to unseen languages with near-lossless retention (0.99), indicating that the model operates on language-agnostic semantic geometry rather than surface form. Our results position explicit consolidation over document structure as a compact and traceable alternative to scale for multilingual legal summarization.
2609.27032.title: LexLattice: Multilingual Extractive Summarization via Neural Cellular Automata on Document Hierarchies

2609.27387.abstract: AraGenre is a shared task on hierarchical, definition-guided Arabic genre classification, motivated by the limited availability of annotated data in Arabic and other low-resource languages. Systems assign each Arabic text segment both a broad communicative genre and a fine-grained specific genre. The released training and development sets contain limited, primarily synthetic and controlled examples, whereas the hidden final benchmark contains noisier naturally occurring text spanning Modern Standard Arabic, Classical Arabic, and multiple dialects. Participants received natural-language definitions for 74 previously unseen specific genres, creating a zero-shot label generalisation setting in which systems had to infer class semantics rather than memorise fixed label-feature associations. The task attracted 46 registrations and 373 submissions, with 17 teams completing the final evaluation. Thakaa ranked first with a Hierarchical Macro F1 of 0.7352, followed by HoangPhong (HP) with 0.7169 and NAMAA with 0.7013. The results show strong broad-genre recognition but a substantial gap in fine-grained classification under linguistic and domain variation.

key_points: AraGenre evaluated hierarchical and definition-guided Arabic genre classification.
The setup tested zero-shot label generalisation using natural-language definitions for 74 unseen specific genres.
The evaluation included Modern Standard Arabic, Classical Arabic, and multiple dialects.
Thakaa ranked first among 17 participating teams with a Hierarchical Macro F1 of 0.7352.
en.summary:
Arabic text classification faces challenges due to limited annotated data, particularly across various dialects and linguistic registers. To address this, the AraGenre shared task challenged participants to perform hierarchical genre classification using natural-language definitions for unseen genres rather than relying on fixed label-feature memorisation.

The evaluation featured datasets containing synthetic training examples and a noisier natural test set spanning Modern Standard Arabic, Classical Arabic, and multiple dialects. Thakaa secured first place with a Hierarchical Macro F1 of 0.7352, demonstrating strong broad-genre recognition while revealing performance gaps in fine-grained classification.
en.tldr: AraGenre 2026 is a shared task evaluating hierarchical, definition-guided Arabic genre classification in a zero-shot label generalisation setting.

glossary.explanation_id: Kompetisi bersama di antara para peneliti untuk menyelesaikan tugas NLP menggunakan set data standar yang sama.
Kemampuan model untuk mengenali dan menggeneralisasi label kelas baru tanpa pelatihan contoh sebelumnya.
Metrik evaluasi yang menghitung rata-rata skor F1 secara hierarkis pada berbagai tingkat kategori.
Bentuk standar bahasa Arab yang digunakan secara luas dalam tulisan dan media formal modern.
Bentuk historis bahasa Arab yang digunakan dalam teks-teks keagamaan dan sastra klasik.

key_points: AraGenre mengevaluasi klasifikasi genre bahasa Arab yang bersifat hierarkis dan dipandu definisi.
Pengaturan eksperimen menguji *zero-shot label generalisation* menggunakan definisi teks untuk 74 genre spesifik yang belum pernah dilihat.
Evaluasi mencakup *Modern Standard Arabic*, *Classical Arabic*, dan berbagai dialek bahasa Arab.
Tim Thakaa meraih peringkat pertama dari 17 tim yang menyelesaikan evaluasi akhir dengan skor *Hierarchical Macro F1* 0,7352.
id.summary:
Klasifikasi teks bahasa Arab menghadapi kendala akibat keterbatasan data ber-*anotasi*, terutama pada ragam dialek dan variasi linguistik. Untuk mengatasi hal tersebut, *shared task* AraGenre menantang peserta melakukan klasifikasi genre hierarkis menggunakan definisi bahasa alami untuk genre baru tanpa mengandalkan hafalan label.

Evaluasi ini menggunakan set pelatihan sintetis serta set uji alami yang mencakup *Modern Standard Arabic*, *Classical Arabic*, dan berbagai dialek. Tim Thakaa menduduki peringkat pertama dengan *Hierarchical Macro F1* sebesar 0,7352, menunjukkan pengenalan genre luas yang kuat tetapi menyisakan celah pada klasifikasi tingkat lanjut.
id.tldr: AraGenre 2026 adalah *shared task* untuk klasifikasi genre bahasa Arab berbasis definisi hierarkis dalam pengaturan *zero-shot label generalisation*.

2609.27387.title: AraGenre 2026: A Hierarchical Definition-Guided Arabic Genre Classification Shared Task

2609.27758.abstract: Safety alignment in large language models is trained primarily in English, and recent work reports that the underlying harmfulness representation survives translation: English-trained probes separate harmful from harmless prompts almost as well in low-resource languages as in English. This has been taken as evidence that cross-lingual refusal failures mainly reflect calibration rather than representation quality. We show that this conclusion depends on the choice of negative examples. Across nine languages spanning three resource tiers, we replicate near-perfect transfer (AUROC > 0.98) when harmless prompts come from an unrelated distribution (easy negatives). With XSTest contrast prompts, which are benign but surface-similar to harmful requests (hard negatives), transfer collapses in low-resource languages while remaining largely stable in high-resource languages. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, mean AUROC drop increases from 0.003 in English to 0.017 in high-resource, 0.042 in mid-resource, and 0.276 in low-resource languages. The pattern replicates on Aya Expanse. Back-translation chrF controls and a matched-chrF comparison across three languages reduce the likelihood that translation quality explains the effect. The collapse remains after controlling for chrF (partial r = 0.70, p = 0.03). Tokenizer fertility correlates with the collapse and explains part of the resource-tier effect, but not all of it. The results show that easy-negative transfer can coexist with substantial degradation under hard negatives. Easy-negative evaluation alone therefore cannot establish that the harmfulness representation survives translation.

key_points: Prior research suggested near-perfect cross-lingual transfer of harmfulness representations using easy negatives.
Using hard negatives from XSTest reveals that transfer collapses in low-resource languages.
The performance drop worsens as language resource tiers decrease, demonstrated on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Aya Expanse.
Controls for translation quality and tokenizer fertility indicate that these factors only partially explain the degradation.
en.summary:
Safety alignment in *large language models* is primarily trained in English, and previous studies suggested that harmfulness representations transfer well to low-resource languages based on evaluations using easy negatives. However, these findings depend heavily on the choice of negative examples.

Evaluating across nine languages spanning three resource tiers using XSTest contrast prompts as hard negatives, this study demonstrates that cross-lingual transfer collapses in low-resource languages while remaining stable in high-resource languages. These findings show that easy-negative evaluations are insufficient to establish whether harmfulness representations truly survive translation.
en.tldr: Safety alignment cross-lingual transfer in large language models relies heavily on negative examples, where hard negatives reveal significant representation degradation in low-resource languages.

glossary.explanation_id: Contoh negatif yang tampak serupa dengan permintaan berbahaya tetapi sebenarnya bersifat jinak.
Contoh negatif dari distribusi yang tidak berkaitan dan sangat mudah dibedakan dari data berbahaya.
Metode atau evaluasi yang melibatkan perpindahan atau penerapan antarbahasa.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur area di bawah kurva karakteristik operasi penerima untuk performa klasifikasi.
Ukuran seberapa banyak token yang dihasilkan oleh *tokenizer* untuk merepresentasikan satu kata atau teks tertentu.
Proses menerjemahkan teks kembali ke bahasa asal untuk menguji kualitas atau konsistensi terjemahan.

key_points: Penelitian sebelumnya melaporkan transfer lintas bahasa yang hampir sempurna menggunakan *easy negatives*.
Penggunaan *hard negatives* dari XSTest membuktikan bahwa transfer representasi runtuh pada bahasa *low-resource*.
Penurunan performa semakin parah pada tingkat sumber daya yang lebih rendah, seperti yang diuji pada model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct dan Aya Expanse.
Faktor kualitas penerjemahan dan *tokenizer fertility* telah dikontrol dan terbukti hanya sebagian yang menjelaskan degradasi tersebut.
id.summary:
*Safety alignment* pada *large language model* umumnya dilatih dalam bahasa Inggris, dan penelitian sebelumnya melaporkan bahwa representasi kebahayaan dapat ditransfer dengan baik ke bahasa *low-resource*. Akan tetapi, kesimpulan ini sangat bergantung pada pemilihan contoh negatif yang digunakan dalam evaluasi.

Dengan menguji sembilan bahasa dari tiga tingkat sumber daya menggunakan *prompt* kontras dari XSTest sebagai *hard negatives*, studi ini menunjukkan bahwa transfer lintas bahasa mengalami kegagalan pada bahasa *low-resource* tetapi tetap stabil pada bahasa *high-resource*. Hasil ini membuktikan bahwa evaluasi menggunakan *easy negatives* saja tidak cukup untuk menyimpulkan bahwa representasi kebahayaan bertahan dengan baik setelah penerjemahan.
id.tldr: *Safety alignment* pada *large language model* menunjukkan degradasi representasi bahaya yang signifikan pada bahasa *low-resource* ketika diuji menggunakan *hard negatives*.

2609.27758.title: Hard Negatives Reveal What Easy Negatives Hide: Cross-Lingual Harmfulness Representations Degrade with Resource Tier Under Hard Negatives

2609.27811.abstract: Online platforms have become arenas for the public contestation of climate change, shaping how scientific knowledge, denial, and uncertainty are expressed and disputed. Yet longitudinal evidence remains limited for YouTube, especially for Portuguese-language discourse. Addressing this gap, we characterize how climate stances are expressed and contested over time in a large corpus of Portuguese-language YouTube comments retrieved through Brazil-oriented climate-related searches. To support this analysis in a noisy, imbalanced, and low-resource setting, we collect more than 240,000 comments posted between 2014 and 2024 and formulate stance detection as a three-way classification task (Believer, Denier, and Inconclusive). We operationalize stance attribution through a scalable self-training pipeline based on Llama 3.1, using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and hybrid instance selection to expand the training set with high-confidence pseudo-labeled examples while preserving class diversity. This approach improves coverage and class balance for minority and rhetorically complex classes, enabling large-scale stance attribution without extensive manual annotation. Our results show that polarisation is marked by interactional asymmetries: denialist comments are less prevalent, but they are associated with a comparatively higher share of cross-stance contestation, while pro-consensus discourse is more strongly reinforced within stance-homogeneous threads.
2609.27811.title: A Decade of Climate Polarization on Brazilian YouTube using Language Models

2609.27814.abstract: In statutory question answering, every claim must be traceable to evidence, not merely relevant, since unverifiable labour-rights answers carry serious legal consequences. Current systems fall short: single-pass RAG cannot detect insufficient evidence, while multi-agent legal-debate systems treat grounding as a prompting convention, letting agents cite unretrieved evidence. To address this gap, we introduce LabourCrew, a multi-agent RAG framework built around three grounding mechanisms: StatuteGraph, a graph index that explicitly links chapter, section, proviso, and cross-reference structure rather than fixed-length spans; an Evidence Exchange Protocol that confines advocates and an interpreter to an evidence ledger, making citation to unretrieved text impossible, while a fault-tolerant supervisor board runs advocates in parallel so individual failures degrade rather than crash the system; and a Calibrated Trust Gate that replaces categorical accept/reject decisions with a trust score, thresholded via conformal risk control for a distribution-free bound on the false-accept rate. We evaluate on LabourActQA, a 500-item Bangla question set from the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, spanning seven reasoning categories and three difficulty tiers. The framework drives the empirical false-accept rate to 0.081, within the target level ($\alpha = 0.10$), achieves the highest Answer Relevancy among HyDE RAG, Graph-RAG, and Hierarchical RAG (0.862 $>$ 0.839, 0.815, 0.828), and degrades gradually rather than catastrophically as question difficulty increases. These results show that calibrated abstention, not retrieval quality alone, is what makes legal question answering auditable in low-resource statutory domains.
2609.27814.title: LabourCrew: A Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Trustworthy Adversarial Deliberation and Statutory Reasoning over Labour Law
